stories.title: Seattle Construction Costs Rise, Bidding Remains Competitive
stories.excerpt: Non-residential construction conditions in the Seattle area remained broadly stable through the first half of 2026, though cost pressures varied significantly by market, trade and project type. According to a recent report by Mortenson, mega-project investments remain the strongest source of upward pressure, while softer demand across portions of the commercial and institutional market continues to create competitive bidding opportunities as trade partners actively pursue available work. Seattle continues to see strong interest from trade partners and competitive bidding, with some firms absorbing market increases or reducing fees to secure work. Despite this competitive environment, pricing increased across several mechanical and specialty scopes this quarter, including plumbing, HVAC and fire protection, contributing to a +1.71% overall quarterly increase.Non-residential construction costs tracked by Mortenson increased 1.71% in Seattle during the quarter and +3.48% over the past twelve months. Nationally, costs increased +1.58% during the quarter and +5.60% over the past twelve months. The post Seattle Construction Costs Rise, Bidding Remains Competitive appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Seattle non-residential construction costs rose 1.71% Q1 2026, 3.48% YoY through Q1.
Mechanical/specialty trades (plumbing, HVAC, fire protection) drove pricing increases despite competitive bidding.
Softer commercial/institutional demand creates bidding pressure; some firms absorbing costs to secure work.
stories.summary: Seattle construction costs increased 1.71% in the first quarter of 2026 and 3.48% over the past twelve months, with particular pressure in mechanical and specialty trades. Despite competitive bidding conditions driven by softer commercial and institutional demand, some trade partners are absorbing cost increases or reducing fees to win projects. Nationally, costs rose 1.58% quarterly and 5.60% annually.
stories.impact: Modest cost inflation in Seattle multifamily development remains manageable given competitive trade pricing, but escalation in specialty mechanical work (HVAC, plumbing, fire protection) will compress margins on new construction starts. Watch for developer pullback if cost growth accelerates; current bidding competition may not persist if demand rebounds.

stories.title: Kirkland & Ellis Hires Seth Niedermayer as Partner in Real Estate Group
stories.excerpt: After more than a decade at HSF Kramer, real estate attorney Seth Niedermayer has moved offices to Kirkland & Ellis. Niedermayer joined the Chicago-based law firm’s real estate group as a partner this week, as shared in a LinkedIn post Monday evening and confirmed by a spokesperson for the firm. Kirkland & Ellis, which serves a range of clients in private equity and corporate transactions, operates a growing New York City practice at its 900 Third Avenue offices as well as an expanding real estate group. At Kirkland & Ellis, Niedermayer will represent private equity and investor clients, as well as developers and operators, across real estate transactions, according to a spokesperson for the firm. His primary focus will be joint ventures and financing. “Kirkland has an unrivaled platform to serve clients on their most sophisticated and important matters, and I’m excited to collaborate with the firm’s exceptionally talented lawyers,” Niedermayer told Commercial Observer in a statement. “I look forward to bringing my experience to the team and continuing to build on the firm’s tremendous momentum in real estate.” Niedermeyer’s move follows more than a decade of work at HSF Kramer, which was still Kramer Levin Naftalis & Frankel when he arrived as an associate in 2015. He had limited real estate experience then, Niedermeyer told CO in June, but the firm’s practice evolved alongside the real estate market — particularly as private capital gained dominance. He was made partner in 2022. During his tenure, Niedermeyer represented Mitsui Fudosan America in its joint venture at 50 Hudson Yards. He also worked on Vici Properties and Apollo Global Management’s acquisition of the Venetian on the Las Vegas Strip in 2022. “For more than a decade, Seth has been a valued member of our real estate practice, and we’re grateful for his contributions to the firm and our clients,” Jay Neveloff, chair of U.S. real estate at HSF Kramer, told CO in a statement.
bullets: Seth Niedermayer joins Kirkland & Ellis as partner in real estate group from HSF Kramer.
Focus areas: joint ventures, financing, private equity and developer/operator transactions.
K&E expanding NYC practice at 900 Third Avenue with growing real estate platform.
stories.summary: Real estate attorney Seth Niedermayer has moved from HSF Kramer to Kirkland & Ellis as a partner in the Chicago-based firm's real estate group. He will represent private equity, investor, developer and operator clients, with primary focus on joint ventures and real estate financing. K&E is expanding its NYC real estate practice.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development markets. This is a law firm hiring story reflecting capital availability and deal velocity in real estate; it signals confidence in financing and JV activity but does not affect supply, demand, costs, or capital flows to multifamily specifically.

stories.title: Realty Income, KKR Establish European Joint Venture
stories.excerpt: Realty Income Corporation and KKR have formed a euro-denominated joint venture that is expected to own a diversified portfolio of existing European net lease real estate assets contributed by Realty Income, spanning four markets and a broad mix of industries and tenants. Capital accounts advised by KKR intend to make an initial investment of €528 million (approximately US$609 million) to acquire a 49% equity interest in the JV, with Realty Income retaining a 51% ownership interest and continuing to manage the portfolio through its European operating platform. “This transaction marks another important step in Realty Income’s evolution as the leading global net lease platform,” said Sumit Roy, Realty Income’s president and CEO. “Building on the private capital foundation we have established in the U.S., our strategic partnership with KKR extends this strategy into Europe and demonstrates both the portability of our competitive advantages across borders and the confidence that leading institutional investors have in our platform.” The transaction is expected to close on Sept. 30. Lazard acted as financial advisor and DLA Piper served as legal advisor to Realty Income. Citi served as financial advisor and Latham & Watkins LLP served as legal advisor to KKR. The post Realty Income, KKR Establish European Joint Venture appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Realty Income and KKR form euro-denominated JV; KKR invests €528M (~$609M) for 49% equity stake.
Realty Income retains 51% ownership, manages European net lease portfolio across four markets.
Transaction closing expected Sept. 30; reflects global capital flowing into stabilized real estate.
stories.summary: Realty Income and KKR have established a European joint venture with KKR investing approximately $609 million for a 49% equity interest in a diversified net lease portfolio. Realty Income retains 51% ownership and ongoing management through its European platform. The transaction demonstrates institutional capital confidence in Realty Income's global platform and is expected to close Sept. 30.
stories.impact: No direct multifamily impact; this is a net lease (retail, office, industrial) capital deployment story. However, it signals that large institutional capital (KKR) remains available for real estate and confident in income-producing assets, which may support financing availability and refinancing appetite for stabilized multifamily assets.

stories.title: Podcast: How AI Is Making Rental Application Fraud Harder to Catch, with Docuverus
stories.excerpt: Jamie Borodin is the founder and CEO of Docuverus, a document verification and fraud detection platform purpose-built for multifamily housing providers. With over 30 years in resident screening, Jamie founded Docuverus in 2017 to address a gap no existing tool was solving: authenticating income documents at the metadata level while simultaneously reading and calculating their contents. Docuverus is one of the only platforms with a direct connection to the Social Security Administration for synthetic identity detection. Jamie is based in southern New Jersey. (02:16) Why standard screening misses income fraud (05:03) How fraud evolved from COVID to AI-generated documents (07:13) What a sophisticated fake pay stub looks like today (09:09) What bad debt files actually reveal (13:10) Operators don’t know how much bad debt is fraud (14:12) False security: when your PMS fraud tool isn’t enough (18:27) Why bank account linking isn’t fraud detection (19:11) Fraud hotspots: Houston, Atlanta, and why NYC is different (24:27) Social Security fraud and synthetic identity detection (25:36) What a CPN is and how it fabricates a credit file (27:58) Florida’s felony law and the limits of regulation (29:29) Screening compliance: why the liability falls on the operator (33:27) Where fraud prevention goes as AI lowers the barrier (35:42) Collaboration superpower: Albert Einstein Learn more: –Visit Docuverus –Jamie Borodin on LinkedIn –Sales line –Multifamily Applicant Fraud Trends Report: Q2 2026 Virtual Events: –AI & Innovation Forum: Multifamily: on 9/29 –SFR / BTR Forum: on 10/22 In-person Events: –Institutional Investors & PE Forum: in NYC on 9/16 –South Florida Capital & Development Forum: in Miami on 10/15 –Finance Forum: in NYC on 11/3 –All upcoming Commercial Observer events Connect with Tangent: -Edward Cohen on LinkedIn -Zach Aarons on LinkedIn -Tangent on LinkedIn
bullets: Docuverus CEO Jamie Borodin discusses AI-enabled rental application fraud detection challenges.
Fraud hotspots identified: Houston, Atlanta; NYC exhibits different patterns; synthetic identity fraud rising.
Standard screening tools and PMS fraud detection insufficient; AI-generated fake documents evade detection.
stories.summary: A podcast discussion featuring Docuverus founder Jamie Borodin explores how AI-generated documents and evolving fraud tactics are outpacing traditional rental application screening. Fraud hotspots include Houston and Atlanta; NYC shows different patterns. Standard screening tools and property management system fraud detection are inadequate against synthetic identity fraud and AI-fabricated pay stubs.
stories.impact: Elevated resident screening risk in high-fraud submarkets (Houston, Atlanta) raises bad debt exposure for new multifamily stabilization; developers and operators must budget for higher credit losses and more sophisticated verification infrastructure. This creates competitive advantage for operators with advanced fraud detection and underwriting discipline in these markets.

stories.title: Target to Add Austin-Area Store
stories.excerpt: Target Corp. plans to open a new store at a 75-acre retail development in Bastrop. The store, slated to go in at State Highway 71 and Farm to Market Road 969, is about 35 miles east of Austin. The retail center, Sendero, could feature 250,000 square feet of retail and restaurant space, 782 apartments, a hotel and over 100,000 square feet of medical and wellness office space once complete. The Austin Business Journal reports that Bastrop is considering an economic incentive package for Pearl River Cos., the developer of Sendero. Target has added locations in Liberty Hill and Dripping Springs, besides the store under consideration in Bastrop. Bastrop, and Bastrop County have about 119,000 citizens. Sendero’s tenants include Chuy’s, Westlake Dermatology & Cosmetic Surgery, Jersey Mike’s, Einstein Bros. Bagels, Texas Roadhouse, Scooter’s Coffee and a dual-branded Marriott hotel. The post Target to Add Austin-Area Store appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Target opening new store in Bastrop retail development (SHwy 71/FM 969), 35 miles east of Austin.
Mixed-use project Sendero: 250K SF retail/restaurant, 782 apartments, hotel, 100K+ SF medical/wellness office.
Bastrop County (~119K population) receiving economic incentive package from Pearl River Cos. developer.
stories.summary: Target Corp. plans a new store within Sendero, a 75-acre mixed-use development in Bastrop, Texas, approximately 35 miles east of Austin. The project will include 250,000 square feet of retail and restaurant space, 782 apartments, a hotel, and over 100,000 square feet of medical/wellness office space. Bastrop County is considering economic incentives for developer Pearl River Cos.
stories.impact: Target's anchor tenant commitment signals retail/lifestyle confidence in exurban Austin growth corridor (Bastrop County); the 782-unit apartment component suggests developer confidence in workforce housing demand 35 miles east of the CBD. This validates outward population/employment migration from core Austin and points to pent-up demand for value-oriented multifamily in suburban Austin periphery; primary market risk is absorption pace given distance from employment centers and the COVID-era hollowing of retail.

stories.title: GTIS Rebrands as Brightshore Capital, Launches Credit Fund
stories.excerpt: GTIS Partners LP said Tuesday it has rebranded as Brightshore Capital LP, following the 21-year-old real estate investment firm’s transition to 100% ownership by its partners. The firm also announced the launch of Brightshore Credit, a real estate debt investment platform anchored with a $250-million investment that will focus on origination and investment in high-yield credit including stretch senior and mezzanine financings, preferred equity and B-notes. “The Brightshore name reflects who we are today: a partner-owned investment firm with over 20 years of experience and a long-term commitment to our investors,” said Tom Shapiro, president and founder of Brightshore Capital. “With the firm now fully owned by the partners who have built and led the business, this is the right moment to establish an identity that is entirely our own and reflects where we are taking the business next.” Brightshore manages $5.6 billion in gross assets, focusing on residential and industrial investments in the U.S. and residential, industrial, office and hospitality in Brazil. The post GTIS Rebrands as Brightshore Capital, Launches Credit Fund appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: GTIS Partners rebrands to Brightshore Capital LP following 100% partner buyout after 21 years.
Launches Brightshore Credit: $250M real estate debt fund (stretch senior, mezz, preferred equity, B-notes).
Brightshore manages $5.6B gross assets; focuses on U.S. residential/industrial and Brazilian real estate.
stories.summary: GTIS Partners has rebranded as Brightshore Capital LP following full partner ownership transition. The firm concurrently launched Brightshore Credit, a real estate debt investment platform anchored with $250 million in capital targeting high-yield credit strategies including stretch senior, mezzanine, preferred equity and B-notes. Brightshore manages $5.6 billion in gross assets across U.S. and Brazilian real estate.
stories.impact: New $250M credit platform and partner ownership recapitalization signals confidence in distressed/complex multifamily debt opportunities and preferred equity demand. This capital may support stressed refinancings or subordinated financing for acquisitions, but tight credit box suggests deals must be deep value or sponsor recaps—not a broad-market capital availability signal for stabilized development.

stories.title: Data Center Operator to Begin Work on $399M Corpus Christi Campus
stories.excerpt: Hut 8 Corp. is starting work next week on the Beacon Point data center campus in Nueces County. The 657,130-square-foot facility is estimated to cost $399 million. It hopes to have the facility operational in November of 2027. The facility is planned for 4650 FM 1694 in Robstown. Hut 8 Corp. says Beacon Point will be a 525-acre, AI-focused campus planned for up to 1 gigawatt of capacity. Jacobs Project Management Co. is listed as the design firm. The San Antonio Business Journal reports Hut 8 signed a 15-year lease worth at least $9.8 billion for 352 megawatts of capacity at the Beacon Point campus. Hut 8 also disclosed a second 15-year, 352-megawatt lease at Beacon Point with the same tenant, bringing total contracted capacity to 704 megawatts and total contract value to approximately $19.6 billion. Project partners previously identified by Hut 8 include American Electric Power, Vertiv Holdings Co. and Jacobs. The post Data Center Operator to Begin Work on $399M Corpus Christi Campus appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Hut 8 Corp. breaking ground on $399M Beacon Point data center campus in Nueces County (Robstown).
657K SF facility, 525-acre campus, 1 GW capacity target; operational target Nov. 2027.
Two 15-year leases totaling ~$19.6B contract value for 704 MW of capacity to undisclosed tenant.
stories.summary: Hut 8 Corp. is beginning construction on the Beacon Point AI-focused data center campus in Robstown, Texas (Nueces County), a $399 million project comprising 657,130 square feet on a 525-acre site targeting 1 gigawatt of capacity by November 2027. The company has signed two 15-year leases worth approximately $19.6 billion for 704 megawatts of contracted capacity.
stories.impact: Major employer/infrastructure investment in Corpus Christi/Nueces County region will drive population in-migration, wage growth, and downstream demand for workforce and market-rate multifamily housing. However, project employment (data centers are capital-intensive, labor-light) is modest; secondary effects depend on supply-chain vendor attraction and whether Hut 8 ancillary operations (support staff, HQ functions) migrate to the region. Monitor for population growth and job creation spillover into Corpus Christi proper over 2027–2030.

stories.title: Brooklyn’s Former Hotel Bossert Set to Become Ritz-Carlton Luxury Residences
stories.excerpt: The historic former Hotel Bossert in Brooklyn Heights — once home to the victory party for the Brooklyn Dodgers’ lone World Series win — will now become Ritz-Carlton-branded luxury condos under new ownership. Developer SomeraRoad, which acquired the 14-story, 282-key hotel at 98 Montague Street for $100 million in May 2025, announced Tuesday alongside Marriott International that it will redevelop the building into the Ritz-Carlton Residences, Brooklyn Heights. “The Hotel Bossert has long stood as one of Brooklyn’s most iconic buildings, and we are honored to help write its next chapter,” Ian Ross, founder and managing principal of SomeraRoad, said in a statement. “We are thoughtfully restoring this historic property while creating a residential experience that honors the Bossert’s rich legacy and celebrates the enduring appeal of Brooklyn Heights. We believe this project will become Brooklyn’s premier residential address and stand among the finest new residential offerings in New York City.” A spokesperson for SomeraRoad declined to provide information on the number of residential units planned for the new development, but in a 5 Questions interview with Commercial Observer in December 2025, Ross said the project will “be 70 luxury, top-of-market, insanely amenitized, branded condos.” The new project will also offer hospitality services and amenities focused on wellness, leisure and entertainment. Plus, residents will be able to dine at a brand-new restaurant coming to the base of the hotel redevelopment. In May, Danny Meyer’s Union Square Hospitality Group signed a 3,200-square-foot lease to open a new restaurant at the property, though details about the future eatery are unclear. SomeraRoad, which has more than 130 investments in over 50 markets across the U.S., bought the former hotel stretching the length of Hicks Street between Montague and Remsen streets from former lender Beach Point Capital. bullets: SomeraRoad acquired Hotel Bossert (14-story, 282-key historic hotel, Brooklyn Heights) for $100M in May 2025.
Converting to Ritz-Carlton Residences luxury condos; partnership with Marriott International.
Historic hotel-to-luxury-residential conversion in high-demand Brooklyn Heights submarket.

The 14-story property at 98 Montague Street will preserve the building's historic character while creating premium residential inventory.
stories.impact: Hotel-to-residential conversion reduces net multifamily supply by converting hospitality into for-sale luxury product rather than rental; this is a capital redeployment away from multifamily. However, conversion signals strong Brooklyn Heights condo demand and validates luxury branded residential as an alternative yield asset. For rental developers, it signals potential scarcity premium in prime Brooklyn Heights and potential upside for Class A rental conversions if condo sales slow.

stories.title: Starwood Capital Group Hires Blackstone’s Michael Eglit as U.S. Head of Originations
stories.excerpt: Fall is almost here and a slight chill — plus the scent of freshly sharpened pencils — is in the air. For Starwood Capital Group, there’s also a new leader at the helm of its debt business as the firm gears up for the fourth quarter. Starwood Capital has hired Michael Eglit as its new head of U.S. originations, sources confirmed to Commercial Observer. Previously, Eglit spent almost 15 years at Blackstone, most recently as head of U.S. originations for Blackstone Real Estate Debt Strategies. Commercial Mortgage Alert reported last month that the move was in the works. Eglit’s first day was Sept. 8 — he’ll be splitting his time between Greenwich, Conn., and New York City — and his move comes roughly 17 months after Jonathan Pollack, Eglit’s former Blackstone colleague, joined Starwood Capital Group as president. With that familiarity as the foundation, sources familiar with the move said that Eglit becoming part of the Starwood team was a very natural fit from a cultural point of view. As one source put it, “Starwood’s got one of the most pre-eminent debt businesses in the country, and Mike’s goal is to now come in and help make it even bigger and better.” Eglit brings plenty of new relationships to Starwood’s table, the source said, adding that the majority of Starwood’s loans are to repeat borrowers and the firm has lost its fair share to Blackstone as a competitor over the years. Now Eglit can bring some of those relationships Starwood couldn’t penetrate into the fold. “People do business with people that they know, they like and they trust, and Starwood just added that additional element in those relationships that didn’t exist before, which will be impactful to their business,” the source said, adding that the team is already looking at deals that they’ve never looked at or won previously with Eglit onboard. bullets: Michael Eglit hired by Starwood Capital Group as head of U.S. originations for real estate debt.
Eglit departed Blackstone after ~15 years as head of U.S. originations for BREDS; started Sept. 8.
Follows Jonathan Pollack's move to Starwood Capital as president ~17 months prior; cultural/team continuity.
stories.summary: Starwood Capital Group hired Michael Eglit as head of U.S. real estate originations effective Sept. 8, recruiting him from Blackstone Real Estate Debt Strategies where he served as head of U.S. originations for approximately 15 years. The hire follows a similar move by Jonathan Pollack (Eglit's former Blackstone colleague) to Starwood as president about 17 months earlier, suggesting deliberate team building.
stories.impact: Starwood Capital, a preeminent real estate debt platform, is doubling down on origination firepower; this signals aggressive growth in debt capital deployment and origination discipline. For multifamily developers, this expands senior and subordinated financing sources and competition for deal flow, potentially tightening spreads and improving execution certainty on debt raises—positive for multifamily capital availability in competitive debt markets.

stories.title: Market Shifts, New York’s Uniqueness Mean Mamdani’s Grocery Plan Could Work
stories.excerpt: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani wants to get the city into the subsidized grocery business. As his administration seeks a seasoned partner this fall to run its planned quintet of government-supported grocery stores, strong opposition means it won’t sail through the express checkout lane. Plus, a pair of new lawsuits could stop the scheme faster than you can cancel an Instacart order, and many critics decry the initiative as the first step in a descent into socialism. Yet, commercial real estate and grocery pros say the idea could work, though key business and financial details remain to be settled. The suits were filed weeks after the administration opened up bidding for a private-sector operator to run five planned stores, one in each borough, and seasoned grocery industry veterans may be in the mix to be part of one of the most high-profile measures in the mayor’s agenda to possibly make life in New York less expensive. Mamdani announced the initiative early in his term, later specifying that city stores would discount prices by 30 percent on essentials such as produce, meat and seafood, and by 20 percent on items including milk and bread. The stores won’t sell alcohol, tobacco or nicotine, but will stock halal, kosher, diabetic-friendly and gluten-free products. Mamdani says this will cut the average New Yorker’s grocery bill by about $90 a month — roughly $1,000 a year. “In the wealthiest city, in the wealthiest country in the history of the world, no New Yorker should have to worry about being able to afford to feed their family,” Mamdani said in a July 27 press conference announcing the request for proposals by the New York City Economic Development Corporation (NYCEDC). Prospective operators of the five planned stores can submit plans until Oct. 16, the agency said. Two sites were already public as of the end of August: La Marqueta, a roughly 9,000-square-foot Manhattan location in East Harlem, and a planned 20,000-square-foot store at the Peninsula
bullets: NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani launching five city-owned subsidized grocery stores (30% produce/meat/bread/milk discount).
Seeking private-sector operator partner fall 2025; lawsuits challenging initiative; one store per NYC borough.
Commercial RE/grocery pros say feasible but key business and financial details unresolved.
stories.summary: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani is pursuing a city-owned, subsidized grocery store initiative—five locations (one per borough) offering 30% discounts on staple categories. The administration is soliciting a private-sector operator partnership this fall. The plan faces legal challenges and political opposition, though real estate and grocery industry observers believe the concept is viable, pending resolution of financial and operational details.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact unless subsidized groceries materially affect neighborhood affordability narratives or property values in underserved neighborhoods (likely none). Regulatory/political signal: aggressive municipal intervention in retail/consumer pricing suggests risk of future rent regulation or tenant-favorable policy in NYC. Long-term, subsidized groceries may stabilize lower-income residential demand, supporting Value and Workforce multifamily valuations in targeted boroughs.
